Looping in Security (Ethan) because pattern looks suspicious. Summary of what I see:
- Three separate trial-credit requests over the last 30 days tied to the same company name but submitted from distinct gmail domains and two different billing emails.
- IP and user-agent fingerprints show overlaps during the spike window.
- One of the accounts requested a second extension 48 hours after we approved the first.

I’ve attached the consolidated request log (trial-request-log.pdf). My recommendation: pause any additional free credit issuance until Security confirms this is legitimate expansion. If it’s a genuine POC, we can fast-track a short-term paid pilot (credit-card or PO) to reduce abuse risk.

Ben — please flag this in HubSpot under deal DB-8472 and add the evidence. Nikhil — external comms should be careful and not accuse fraud; offer the procurement route as an alternate.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Jordan — thanks for the context and the attachment. I’m Ethan from Redwood Security. We reviewed the logs Marissa shared. Two points:

1) At this time we see indicators that multiple trial requests are being initiated from the same IP range and there are repeated short-lived accounts that request consecutive extensions. That pattern matches automated or coordinated attempts to extend free-tier usage beyond intended POC scale.

2) We absolutely want to support legitimate evaluations. To proceed safely we can either:
   - Provision a one-time 25k token bridging credit while we complete additional verification (billing domain confirmation + a short screencast showing intended integration), or
   - Move directly to a short paid pilot (30-day paid pilot with an upfront card or PO).

Please let us know which option MerchantsBurst prefers. If you choose the bridging credit, send the verification items to security@redwood.ai and we’ll unlock the tokens within 24 hours pending review.

Best,
Ethan Park
Security Operations
Redwood Inference
